dedupe_keys.name: oasis loss modelling framework oasis lmf

description: The Oasis Loss Modelling Framework is an open-source platform for developing, deploying and running catastrophe loss models, created and maintained by Oasis LMF, a not-for-profit organisation funded by the insurance industry. It provides a web user interface and an API for running models at scale, the ktools core components and standard data formats for hazard and vulnerability, and the oasislmf Python model development kit, a command-line toolkit that generates keys from exposure, builds Oasis input files and computes ground-up, insured and reinsurance losses from exposure in the Open Exposure Data (OED) format. Models are packaged in a standard format and components may come from vendors, academic groups or public bodies; the site reports an ecosystem of more than 18 suppliers covering over 90 models, and PiWind is the public test model. The software is free to use; oasislmf 2.5.7 (August 2026) is on PyPI under BSD-3-Clause, with yearly stable versions and monthly patches. Caveats: most production models in the ecosystem are commercial and licensed separately, and the framework expects insurance-style exposure and financial terms, so infrastructure networks must be represented as locations. It supports hazard exposure and financial risk analysis of infrastructure portfolios and climate adaptation; related records are CLIMADA and the OpenQuake Engine.
